bug_description.normalized: The staged 32759-byte witness is copied into the static global request buffer `data_copy[32767]` and admitted far enough for `parse_http_request()` to call `parse_headers()`. `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` treats the late malformed line beginning with `if-M` as the `If-M` header family, and `HEADER("If-Modified-Since")` rechecks `: ` at offsets 32736..32737, materializes `helper->if_modified_since.raw` as `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` and `raw.len = 17`, and overwrites the original line terminator at offset 32755 from `\r` to `\0`. Vulnerable `parse_if_modified_since()` rejects only `raw.len == 0`, so it still calls `lwan_parse_rfc_time(raw.value, &parsed)` without checking for the full 29-byte RFC1123 form. Inside `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`, the weekday/day/month/year path accepts `Mon,`, `18 `, `Oct `, and the first four year bytes `2777`; its blind `str += 5` steps skip the intervening `0x9c` byte and the fifth `7`, so `str` lands on the NUL written at `data_copy + 32755`. The hour/min/sec `parse_2_digit_num()` calls then fail on that inserted NUL, the later `:` at `data_copy + 32758`, and the zero-filled tail, but lines 98, 100, and 102 still execute `str += 3`. The saved ASan stack therefore pinpoints the final `STRING_SWITCH(str)` at `lwan_parse_rfc_time:104`, which calls `string_as_int32()` with `str = data_copy + 32764` and reads 4 bytes through byte 32767, one byte past global `data_copy`. The patch fixes this exact missing obligation by requiring `helper->if_modified_since.raw.len == sizeof("Wed, 17 Apr 2019 13:59:27 GMT") - 1` before calling the parser.

source.description: First non-harness parser statement that turns attacker-controlled request bytes into the vulnerability-relevant `If-Modified-Since` pointer/length pair.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `gt_results/arvo_14297/poc` is 32759 bytes long. In its exact tail, bytes 32719..32722 are `if-M`, bytes 32736..32737 are `: `, and byte 32755 is `\r` before the vulnerable `HEADER("If-Modified-Since")` macro rewrites that terminator to `\0`.
source.note: Because `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` case-folds the leading `if-M` family and `HEADER` then rechecks only the later `: ` position, the malformed witness line is still treated as `If-Modified-Since`. The assignment on line 585 yields `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` and `raw.len = 17`; the following fine-trace step records the same macro's in-place `*end = '\0'` write at offset 32755.

root_cause.description: The guard rejects only an empty header value. Any non-zero `If-Modified-Since` length, including the witness's short value, is still passed into the fixed-width RFC time parser.
root_cause.note: The patch introduces `header_len = sizeof("Wed, 17 Apr 2019 13:59:27 GMT") - 1` and changes this obligation to `helper->if_modified_since.raw.len != header_len`, so the short witness value would return before `lwan_parse_rfc_time()` is called.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The final line-104 `STRING_SWITCH(str)` probe in `lwan_parse_rfc_time()` reaches this helper with `s = data_copy + 32764`, so the 4-byte read crosses the end of global `data_copy`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` here and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global `data_copy` defined in `fuzz_parse_http_request` line 1621. Frame #1 names `lwan_parse_rfc_time:104`, so the precise internal caller is the final `STRING_SWITCH(str)` probe that checks for `GMT\0` after the short header path has advanced `str` to `data_copy + 32764`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Materializes the staged witness into the exact global array later named by ASan and preserves the copied byte count that bounds header scanning.
tainted_value_origin.note: For the saved PoC, `length = 32759` and the copy populates `data_copy[0..32758]`. ASan identifies this same static object, `data_copy[32767]`, as the overread global.

parser_admitted.description: The vulnerable helper chain only runs after the request parser accepts the copied buffer. The saved ASan stack includes `parse_if_modified_since` at line 1652 inside this branch, so the witness definitely passed the earlier finalizer and `parse_http_request()` checks needed to reach the `If-Modified-Since` parser.

coarse_trace.summary: The 32759-byte witness is copied into global `data_copy[32767]`, and the parser helper exposes the copied buffer and length to the HTTP request parser.

A malformed late header line is still recognized as the `If-Modified-Since` family, and `parse_headers()` materializes `helper->if_modified_since.raw.value/raw.len` from bytes near the end of `data_copy` while also NUL-terminating that short value in place.
Because the raw header length is merely non-zero, `parse_if_modified_since()` calls `lwan_parse_rfc_time()` instead of rejecting the short header.

Inside `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`, the short header advances `str` first to the inserted NUL at offset 32755 and then through later failed hour/min/sec parses to `data_copy + 32764`, where the final line-104 `STRING_SWITCH(str)` issues a 4-byte `string_as_int32()` probe past the end of `data_copy`.

fine_trace.note: Copies the staged witness into the static global request buffer that ASan later names as the overflowed object. For this run, `length = 32759`, so the copied request occupies `data_copy[0..32758]` and bytes `data_copy[32759..32766]` remain zero from the global initializer inside the 32767-byte array.

Exposes the copied bytes to `parse_http_request()` as a bounded parser buffer. Downstream scans in `parse_headers()` use `helper->buffer->value + helper->buffer->len` as `buffer_end`, so header discovery is limited to the first 32759 copied bytes and the `\r` at offset 32755 is found as the line end for the late malformed header.

Source. `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` case-folds the witness bytes at offsets 32719..32722, so the malformed line beginning `if-M` still matches the `If-M` header family. The `HEADER("If-Modified-Since")` macro then rechecks `: ` at offsets 32736..32737 and materializes `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` and `raw.len = 17` from the short value bytes `Mon,\x9c18 Oct 27777`.

Before returning that `struct lwan_value`, the same macro writes `*end = '\0'`. In the staged witness this overwrites the original `\r` at `data_copy + 32755`, so the later time parser receives a NUL-terminated buffer `Mon,\x9c18 Oct 27777\0` at `raw.value`.

Root cause. The only admission check is `raw.len != 0`, so the short 17-byte source value from step 3 is still treated as parseable. The fix changes this to an exact 29-byte length check for the RFC1123 form `Wed, 17 Apr 2019 13:59:27 GMT`.

Because step 5 allows the short header, the caller passes only `raw.value` into `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`. The separate `raw.len` is dropped, so the callee receives a bare pointer even though its parameter type `const char in[static 30]` assumes a full RFC time string plus terminator.

Inside `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`, the first `STRING_SWITCH(str)` accepts `Mon,`; the blind `str += 5` at line 65 skips byte `0x9c` at offset 32742, `parse_2_digit_num()` then accepts `18 `, the month switch accepts `Oct `, and `parse_int(strndupa(str, 4), -1)` uses the first four year bytes `2777`. After the later line-95 `str += 5`, `str` has advanced from `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` to `data_copy + 32755`, which is the NUL written by step 4 over the original `\r`.

At `data_copy + 32755` the hour parse fails immediately on the inserted NUL, but line 98 still executes `str += 3`, moving `str` to `data_copy + 32758` where the later `:` from trailing bytes `oN:` makes the minute parse fail. Lines 100 and 102 likewise keep incrementing after failure, so `str` advances to `data_copy + 32761` and then `data_copy + 32764` inside the zero-filled tail left beyond `length`.

Sink. Frame #1 of the saved ASan stack identifies the caller as `lwan_parse_rfc_time:104`, so this invocation comes from the final `STRING_SWITCH(str)` probe after step 8. With `s = data_copy + 32764`, `memcpy(&i, s, 4)` reads zero-tail bytes 32764..32766 and then byte 32767, which is one past the 32767-byte global object and triggers the reported 4-byte global-buffer-overflow read.

format.contract: The exact witnessed trigger is the staged 32759-byte byte stream whose late header line begins with `if-M` at offsets 32719..32722, has `: ` at offsets 32736..32737, and has original line terminator `\r` at offset 32755. Vulnerable `HEADER("If-Modified-Since")` materializes `helper->if_modified_since.raw` with `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` and `raw.len = 17`, then rewrites byte 32755 to `\0`. Because vulnerable `parse_if_modified_since()` only rejects `raw.len == 0`, it still calls `lwan_parse_rfc_time(raw.value, &parsed)`. That parser advances `str` first to the inserted NUL at `data_copy + 32755`, then through the later `:` and zero tail to `data_copy + 32764`, and its final line-104 `STRING_SWITCH(str)` probe invokes `string_as_int32()`, whose 4-byte read crosses one byte past global `data_copy`.
